note: Faithful rendering of a dense causal argument (fire/smoke, Indra's head); objections and replies are correctly attributed.

errors.english: inscribed with the name of the prince Śakaladhara Fragment-Holder
errors.why: The Tibetan does not call Śakaladhara a prince; he is the powerful figure (a minister) who later complains that the prince robbed him of his lordship, so 'the prince' misidentifies him.

note: Prose narrative is sound; the gnomic verses are rendered loosely but defensibly.
Accurate on cetanā/cetayitvā karma, the Supreme Sage gloss and the root-verse lemmata; only stray inline glosses.

span_why: The opening sentence ('You are impure ... it is also the very same downfall') translates the last line of the previous side.

errors.english: If a monk, with the intention of criticizing, uses insults such as calling someone a donkey
errors.why: The whole side is metrical verse (śloka quatrains) and is rendered as continuous prose.

errors.english: they obtain the downfall of causing exhaustion [note: referring to a specific class of legal disputes that exhaust the community's harmony]
errors.why: This is the pātayantika for reviling/complaining about a formal act of the Saṅgha (ལས་ལ་སྐྱོ་སྔོགས); the note invents a class of disputes, and 'causing a disturbance' misrenders the complaint.

errors.english: Regarding this, if one says: This is good, but even while finished, if one causes a disturbance through doubt, it is accompanied by a downfall.
errors.why: The verse says that if the act was completed with 'good' (sādhu) having been declared, complaining about it even out of doubt incurs the downfall; the English misparses the condition.

errors.english: The learned ones have said that it is not otherwise.
errors.why: The verse says the doubtful complaint is a wrongdoing and NOT the other offense (the pātayantika); 'not otherwise' says the opposite.

fix.find: The learned ones have said that it is not otherwise.
fix.replace: The learned ones have said that it is not the other offense (the downfall).

note: Content is broadly followed, but the verse is flattened into prose, starts with the previous side, and several Vinaya rulings are garbled.
Faithful rendering of the five modes of Prātimokṣa recitation and the reciter's, elder's and middle monk's duties.

errors.english: uttered various doubts and lamentations about what had truly occurred
errors.why: Tibetan (Skt. abhūtārtha-vikalpa-jalpa) says they spoke out imaginings about unreal matters, not about what had truly occurred.

errors.english: they have no regard for anything but the wealth they desire
errors.why: The line (Skt. na kāmakāmasya dhane 'nurodhaḥ) says one who longs for pleasures has no regard for wealth, the reverse of the English.

fix.find: they have no regard for anything but the wealth they desire
fix.replace: one who longs for pleasures has no regard for wealth

errors.english: For those whose deeds are unfinished...
errors.why: The Tibetan of this line (གང་དོན་སློང་...) means 'for whose sake' the petitioners...; nothing about unfinished deeds.

note: The laments are rendered with feeling, but the gnomic contrasts in the third verse are inverted or invented.

errors.english: used because of the desire to express clarity
errors.why: གསལ་བ here is vyakti, 'individual instances': the plural is used because the individuals are meant.

fix.find: used because of the desire to express clarity
fix.replace: used because the individual instances (vyakti) are meant

errors.english: the very mental consciousness that forms the connection is the mind
errors.why: སེམས་དཔའ is sattva, 'the being': the rebirth-linking mental consciousness is the being, not 'the mind'.

fix.find: forms the connection is the mind

errors.english: makes the state of destruction occur
errors.why: The Tibetan says the support brings about the persistence (sthiti) of the perishing thing, not the occurrence of destruction.

fix.find: makes the state of destruction occur
fix.replace: brings about the persistence of what perishes

errors.english: because that which causes destruction does not remain, as it remains of its own accord
errors.why: The sense is: when the destroyer is absent, the thing remains by itself, so a cause of persistence is pointless; the English misattaches the clauses.

errors.english: is indeed spoken of as the very model of the mind
errors.why: The Tibetan says the mind (cognition) is stated as the example, not that something is the model of the mind.

note: The argument on support and persistence is repeatedly misread and two technical terms (vyakti, sattva) are wrong.

errors.english: has committed an offense requiring a formal meeting of the community
errors.why: The Tibetan specifies a CONCEALED saṃghāvaśeṣa offense (བཅབས་པ), which is what brings the community's sanction.

fix.find: has committed an offense requiring a formal meeting of the community
fix.replace: has concealed an offense requiring a formal meeting of the community

note: Accurate on the niśraya duties, the ten-year rule and the pentads; one Vinaya qualifier dropped.

errors.english: possessing number is also impossible for them, because these two
errors.why: གྲངས་དང་ལྡན་པ is 'number and conjunction (saṃyoga)', the two Vaiśeṣika qualities the following 'these two' refers to.

fix.find: possessing number is also impossible for them
fix.replace: number and conjunction are also impossible for them

note: The regress argument against the Vaiśeṣika is well rendered; one category term misread.
Faithful rendering of the non-apprehension and final-complex argument, with the Mīmāṃsaka target correctly identified.
